narrative.what_i_did:
The operator asked to build a real in-app camera and link it into messaging and anywhere else photos are used — the follow-on the previous session had captured after grounding that no in-app camera existed. I re-grounded against the actual code and found two load-bearing facts. First, the wallet ALREADY has a working getUserMedia surface: QrScanModal runs a live video stream with facingMode, a cancelled-flag cleanup, and — critically — a documented caveat that on an installed iOS PWA (exactly how the operator field-tests on the iPhone) live getUserMedia is unreliable and the prompt may never fire, so it defaults that platform to a native-input path. That caveat would have bitten a naive camera build directly, so I designed around it. Second, chat is text-only today: threadMessage.ts marks attachments as an unbuilt 'future' note, and raw photo bytes can't ride NIP-17 relay DMs because of size — so 'use the camera in messages' is a genuine architectural fork, not a wiring task.

I built a dedicated reusable camera feature rather than burying it in an existing one, because the capture feature already depends on journal (so putting the camera there would have made a journal->capture->journal import cycle). src/features/camera/CameraCaptureModal is a pure capture device — it knows nothing about journals or signing, it just returns a JPEG File via onCapture. It opens a live preview with a front/back flip and a shutter that grabs the current video frame to a canvas and encodes JPEG; the front camera preview is CSS-mirrored but the saved frame is unmirrored per selfie convention. The stream lifecycle deps are [facing, useFallback] only, so UI status changes never tear down the stream — a cleaner pattern than the state-driven one in QrScanModal. On installed iOS PWA / missing mediaDevices it goes straight to the native capture input (which DOES open the system camera reliably from a home-screen PWA), and any live-camera error degrades to that same fallback; a choose-from-library path is always offered.

I wired it into the journal composer: a new 📷 Camera button opens the modal, the old library picker became 🖼 Photo, and the captured file flows through the existing onPickAttachment -> normalizeImage -> sign -> anchor -> stamp pipeline unchanged. So 'take it through the app and it stamps it' is now literal — snap a photo in the wallet, it becomes a signed and anchored journal entry, and the stamped-copy share button from the prior cut is right there on its detail. Registered the new feature in features-registry, added a camera bundle-budget entry (measured 1.70KB gz), and updated the manifests and the living-ideas log (the in-app camera moved from sprouting to fruiting). All four gates green, 575 tests. I deliberately did NOT wire the camera into messaging this turn, because that forks on real infrastructure and I put the choice to the operator in chip form rather than guess.
narrative.whats_pending:
The messaging wiring is the open thread, deliberately. Chat has no image support and photos can't travel inside relay DMs, so I surfaced the fork: option A — the chat camera creates a signed+anchored journal entry and shares the stamped copy to the peer via the system sheet, with a verify link dropped in the thread ('we'll just link'), buildable now with no new infra; option B — real in-Tapit image messages that host the encrypted blob and reference it in the DM so it renders in the peer's thread, a bigger cut with its own infrastructure. The operator's chip answer decides the next move. There is also the still-deferred bake-at-capture cosmetic always-on mark from the photo-stamp arc.

The camera itself has had ZERO device validation, and the iOS-PWA path is the one that matters most and is hardest to verify from here. The operator should, on the iPhone, open a journal entry composer, tap 📷 Camera, and confirm that the native camera opens (live preview is expected to be unavailable in the installed PWA, so the fallback 'Take a photo' button should fire the system camera), take a shot, and confirm it lands as an attachment and signs cleanly. On a desktop with a webcam the live preview + flip + shutter path should be exercised separately. The front/back flip and the library path are both unverified in the hand.

The earlier cuts in this arc remain unvalidated on device too: the People-tab secrets condo and the stamped-photo share. The order-dependent identity-gate canonicalization test flake is still latent (suite green).
narrative.what_you_could_do_better: Nothing surfaced beyond the declared scope this session. One small judgment worth recording: I chose a slightly different stream-lifecycle pattern than QrScanModal — deriving UI status without it being an effect dependency — because QrScanModal's pattern (setState inside the effect whose deps include state.kind) looks like it would tear down the stream on the starting->scanning transition. It evidently works there in practice, but I didn't want to copy a pattern I couldn't fully convince myself was correct, so the camera uses [facing, useFallback] as the only stream deps. If a future carpenter unifies the two camera surfaces, that's the cleaner base to converge on. I also left the messaging side unbuilt rather than shipping a half-answer; given the operator's 'use it as well as any other place,' there's a small risk they wanted me to just pick — but the infra fork is real enough that a one-tap chip is the honest path.
narrative.bigger_picture: This is the sovereign-capture loop closing. Until now a verifiable photo had to ENTER the wallet from outside — the OS picker, a file already taken by some other app — and only then could be signed, anchored, and stamped. An in-app camera means the photo is born inside the sovereign boundary: the pixels go straight from the sensor into the signing pipeline without a detour through an untrusted app that could have altered them, and the wallet is the first and only thing that ever held them. That's a meaningfully stronger provenance story than stamping a photo that arrived from who-knows-where, and it's the literal version of the operator's 'take it through the app and it stamps it.' The deliberate decision to build the camera as a pure, dependency-free capture device that every surface links to — rather than a journal feature or a chat feature — is the durable-interface principle again: one camera, many mounts, so messaging and any future surface just import it. And holding the line at the messaging fork rather than bolting raw images into chat protects the same architecture the secrets work protected: chat DMs stay light text envelopes, and heavy verifiable artifacts live as held, anchored attestations that get LINKED into conversations, not stuffed into them. The whole system keeps wanting the same shape — small signed envelopes that reference durable proofs — and the camera feeds that shape rather than fighting it.

feedback_to_appcommander: The grounding-first discipline keeps being the highest-leverage habit: this build's whole shape was determined by two facts that only reading the code surfaces — that QrScanModal already proves the getUserMedia path AND documents that it's unreliable on installed iOS PWAs (the operator's exact field-test platform), and that chat is text-only so 'camera in messages' is an infra fork not a wiring job. A naive camera would have shipped broken on the operator's phone. Worth reinforcing in doctrine: when building a capability, find the nearest existing surface that already does something adjacent (here, the QR scanner's camera) and inherit both its working patterns AND its hard-won caveats. Second pattern: building the camera as a dependency-free, single-purpose feature that every surface links to — chosen specifically to avoid a journal<->capture import cycle — is the reuse-over-duplication principle paying off structurally, and it's why messaging will be a thin mount rather than a second camera. Finally, holding the messaging fork as a chip question instead of bolting raw image bytes into NIP-17 DMs kept the architecture coherent (light text envelopes that LINK to heavy anchored artifacts), which is the same shape the secrets and stamped-photo cuts converged on.
